subject: Re: NovaMed DPIA intake — evidence roadmap and timelines
messages:
From: Dr. Elena Torres <etorres@novamed.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaMed Privacy <privacy@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-04-02T08:14:00+01:00
Subject: NovaMed DPIA intake — request for evidence and next steps

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of NovaMed's onboarding for regulated data we need to complete our DPIA. I've attached our standard DPIA intake spreadsheet (NovaMed_DPIA_Template_v3.docx) — the questions cover lawful basis, data flows, subprocessors, retention and cross-border transfers. A few specific asks up front: 

- Can you provide a data flow diagram (or brief narrative) that captures where PHI/PII enters Redwood, how it's processed (in transit and at rest), and where logs/backups land?
- Confirmation of subprocessors (current list) and whether any processing happens in non-EEA regions; if so, please indicate safeguards (SCCs, BCRs).
- Retention policy for request/response logs, KV cache snapshots, and backups (including RPO/RTO expectations).
- Any standard contractual clauses / DPA references you share with customers.

We'd like an initial response by EOD 2026-04-06 to meet our compliance board window. If you prefer, send a draft and we'll follow up with questions.

Thanks — attaching the template.

Best,
Elena
Dr. Elena Torres
Head of Privacy Operations, NovaMed

Attachment: NovaMed_DPIA_Template_v3.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-04-02T12:30:00+01:00
Subject: Fwd: NovaMed DPIA intake — request for evidence and next steps

Team — forwarding NovaMed's DPIA template. They need an initial response by EOD 2026-04-06. High level asks are in Elena's note; please see attachments. Proposed owners below:

- Rishi: data flows, retention, backups, KV cache lifecycle
- Mina: subprocessors, SCCs, contractual language, evidence index

Key constraints: NovaMed will be processing EU patient data and wants SCCs or equivalent for any non-EEA subprocessors. Also asked about archival backups — they want retention length + location.

Deliverables for 2026-04-06 (draft):
1) Completed DPIA template (answers inline) — Rishi to draft technical responses
2) Evidence index CSV with links to artifacts (SOC 2 report, network diagram screenshots, KMS config, subprocessor list) — Mina to assemble
3) Short narrative data flow (diagram or 2-paragraph summary) — Rishi

If either of you anticipate gaps (e.g., missing screenshots or legal review), flag them now. I'll be available to join a quick sync with NovaMed on 2026-04-05 if necessary.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachment: NovaMed_DPIA_Template_v3.docx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-03T09:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NovaMed DPIA intake — request for evidence and next steps

Lauren / Mina — attaching my draft answers to the technical sections of the DPIA (redwood_dpia_draft_answers.xlsx). Notes / outstanding questions inline: 

- Data flow: primary ingress is via the hosted Redwood API (TLS 1.2+). Processing happens in the customer's chosen region; for NovaMed requested region = eu-west-1. Tokenized request bodies are kept in-memory and streamed; KV cache entries are ephemeral per-session (default TTL 48 hours) unless customer enables long-term cache.
- Logs: request/response logs retained by default for 30 days (configurable via account settings), audit logs (control-plane) retained 365 days. Backups: nightly snapshots of model state and metadata are stored in encrypted S3 buckets; some telemetry backups are replicated to a secondary region for disaster recovery (currently eu-west-1 -> eu-central-1).
- Cross-border: we do use a small set of infra providers with US-based control plane services for hosted onboarding workflows. For processing, we honor region pinning. For any data movements out of EEA, SCCs are applied with subprocessors; need legal to confirm exact clause set.
- Subprocessors: attached sheet includes current public list; I'll add the internal vendor contract IDs.

Outstanding for legal: confirm SCC wording and whether NovaMed needs a DPA amendment for backups that may replicate to a secondary region.

Action items:
- Mina: can you compile the SOC 2 section / evidence links and confirm subprocessor contract references?
- Lauren: can you confirm whether we want to offer a written commitment on retention beyond defaults?

I'll be available for a quick call 2026-04-04 morning to walk through the technical bits.

Regards,
Rishi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpia_draft_answers.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Dr. Elena Torres <etorres@novamed.com>, NovaMed Privacy <privacy@novamed.com>
Date: 2026-04-04T16:45:00+01:00
Subject: Consolidated DPIA response and evidence index — NovaMed

Hi all / Elena —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Attached is the consolidated response pack and an evidence index (evidence_index_20260404.csv) with direct links to artifacts. Summary highlights: 

1) Data flows: included a 2-paragraph narrative and a simplified diagram (internal Drive link in the index). Processing happens in the EU region for NovaMed's account; control-plane telemetry may touch non-EEA infrastructure for onboarding only (see index entry: onboarding-control-plane).
2) Retention: default request logs = 30 days (customer-adjustable), KV cache TTL 48 hours unless explicitly configured for long-lived caching. Backups/snapshots retained 90 days; DR replication between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. We propose a contractual clause to cap backups retention to 90 days for NovaMed if required.
3) Subprocessors & transfers: attached subprocessor list includes vendor IDs and contract status. For any non-EEA subprocessors we will execute SCCs; legal has flagged one vendor for contract amendment — legal will reach out directly if required.
4) Evidence: included links to our SOC 2 Type II summary, network diagram screenshots, KMS key policy export, and encryption-at-rest configuration snippet.

Next steps: 
- Elena / NovaMed: please confirm whether the proposed 90-day backup cap is acceptable or if you require shorter retention.
- I'll coordinate with Legal to finalize SCC wording and provide the DPA excerpt by 2026-04-06 EOD.

Elena: happy to schedule a 30-minute walk-through on Monday 2026-04-05 10:00 CET to step through the answers and artifacts.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Privacy & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence_index_20260404.csv (text/csv), consolidated_dpia_responses.pdf (application/pdf)
